les: Van die see tot in die lug en terug
kaps_punt: Die watersiklus: water verdamp, kondenseer, vries en smelt in die watersiklus

items.bewering: Die water op die aarde beweeg heeltyd van die see na die lug en dan na die land. Dieselfde water loop hierdie pad oor en oor, en ons noem dit die watersiklus.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: WHOI Global Water Cycle (https://www2.whoi.edu/site/globalwatercycle): 86% of evaporation and 78% of precipitation is over the ocean, so the net flow runs from sea to land. Schmitt, Oceanography 21(1) (https://tos.org/oceanography/assets/docs/21-1_schmitt.pdf): about 90% of ocean evaporation rains back on the ocean. The 'pad' image works as the standard route of the cycle. It does not say every drop reaches land, so it is not false. Noted only so a reviser does not harden it into 'all the water'.

items.bewering: By sommige stappe op hierdie pad verander die water van toestand.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: USGS Water Science School (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/sublimation-and-water-cycle) and NSSL; evaporation, condensation, freezing and melting are changes of state, while precipitation and runoff move water without one.

items.bewering: Die son se hitte laat die water in die siklus smelt en verdamp. Water wat weer hitte verloor, kondenseer en vries op ander plekke in die siklus.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): solar energy powers evaporation. USGS (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/sublimation-and-water-cycle): sunlight supplies the energy acting on snow and ice. Losing heat gives condensation and freezing (RMI, https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling).

items.bewering: Die son se hitte en die warm lug dra die water boontoe.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: University of Leeds, atmosphere structure (https://see.leeds.ac.uk/enviroweb/atmosphere/1_structure_and_composition/stru6.php): warmer, more buoyant air rises (convection) and carries the vapour with it. Penn State METEO 3.

items.bewering: Swaartekrag trek die water weer af na 'n laer plek.
items.blok: Water wat dieselfde pad oor en oor loop
items.bron: UCI ESS5 Ch. 7 Precipitation (https://www.ess.uci.edu/~yu/class/ess5/Chapter.7.precipitation.pdf): drops fall once they are too large to stay up. Smithsonian How Things Fly (https://howthingsfly.si.edu/ask-an-explainer/what-gravity-7th-grade-words-and-understanding): gravity draws things toward Earth.

items.bewering: Die son skyn op die see en op die water in damme en riviere. Die son se hitte maak daardie water warmer, en 'n deel daarvan verdamp. Dit gaan as waterdamp die lug bo die see in.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): solar energy powers evaporation from oceans, lakes and soil. USGS water-cycle text reprinted by WaterWorld (https://www.waterworld.com/drinking-water-treatment/article/16206846/usgs-releases-water-cycle-chart).

items.bewering: Waterdamp is water as 'n gas, en jy kan dit glad nie sien nie.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: Scientific American, 'How does bathwater give off steam?' (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/how-does-bathwater-give-off-steam/): the visible 'steam' is liquid droplets. Science Buddies: water in the gas phase is invisible.

items.bewering: Water verdamp ook van nat grond en van nat klere op die lyn.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): evaporation takes moisture from soil. Clothes drying on a line is the same process from a wet surface; see the evaporation-factors sources below.

items.bewering: Hoe warmer die dag is, hoe vinniger verdamp die water.
items.blok: Die son laat die water verdamp
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): 'Temperature, of course, affects how quickly evaporation happens.' This holds as a tendency; wind and humidity also play a part, and the sentence claims nothing against them.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp beweeg saam met die lug na hoër plekke bo die grond. Hoër op is die lug baie kouer as naby die grond.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: Penn State METEO 3 (https://www.e-education.psu.edu/meteo3/print/book/export/html/1968): the average environmental lapse rate is about 6.5 °C per km in the lowest ~10 km. Britannica, 'Lapse rate' (https://www.britannica.com/science/lapse-rate): variable, and local inversions occur, but the general statement holds.

items.bewering: Die damp koel daar af en kondenseer weer tot klein druppels water.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: RMI Belgium, 'Wolkensamenstelling' (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling): excess vapour in saturated air condenses into very small droplets on condensation nuclei. NASA GPM FAQ.

items.bewering: 'n Wolk is nie waterdamp nie, maar 'n klomp van daardie klein druppels.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: NASA GPM FAQ, 'What are clouds made of?' (https://gpm.nasa.gov/resources/faq/what-are-clouds-made-are-they-more-likely-form-polluted-air-or-pristine-air): 'clouds can consist of dry air mixed with liquid water drops, ice particles, or both'; thin, high clouds are mostly ice. RMI Belgium (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling): a cloud is very small droplets OR ice crystals or a mix, and cirrus is ice only. The lesson's own hail block puts frozen ice lumps inside the thunderstorm cloud.
items.regstelling: The first half is right and should stay: a cloud is not water vapour. The second half makes a cloud droplets only, which is too narrow. Narrow the quantifier or name the ice, for example 'maar 'n klomp klein druppels water (en hoog bo ook stukkies ys)', or 'meestal 'n klomp van daardie klein druppels'. The writer chooses the wording, and it must match the 'wolk' glossary entry.

items.bewering: Niemand kan waterdamp sien nie, maar 'n wolk sien jy van ver af.
items.blok: Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp
items.bron: RMI Belgium (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling): the cloud becomes visible once the vapour condenses. Scientific American (bathwater steam).

items.bewering: Waar dit koud genoeg is, vries 'n deel van die water in die siklus.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NSSL Severe Weather 101: Hail (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail); UCI ESS5 Ch. 7 (ice-crystal process at or below freezing).

items.bewering: Hael vorm in 'n donderstorm waar sterk wind die druppels hoog opdra. Die druppels vries daarbo tot ysklonte, en meer water vries laag vir laag daarop.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NSSL Severe Weather 101: Hail (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail): hail forms inside thunderstorm updrafts; raindrops carried up into extremely cold air freeze, then grow as liquid drops freeze onto the surface. NASA GPM FAQ 'How does hail form?' (https://gpm.nasa.gov/resources/faq/how-does-hail-form). 'Sterk wind' for an updraft is acceptable at Grade 4, since the wind does blow upwards.

items.bewering: 'n Ysklont val eers wanneer dit te swaar is vir die wind.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: NSSL hail forecasting (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/forecasting): 'In all cases, the hail falls when the thunderstorm's updraft can no longer support the weight of the ice.' 'Te swaar vir die wind' also covers an updraft that weakens.

items.bewering: In die winter lê sneeu en ys op hoë berge soos die Drakensberg.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage document on uKhahlamba-Drakensberg (https://whc.unesco.org/document/154760): high altitudes get snowfall in winter. SABC News (https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/snow-blankets-drakensberg-peaks-as-temperatures-plunge/) reports snow on the peaks. Peak High Mountaineering (https://peakhigh.co.za/ice-climbing-drakensberg/winter-climbing-destinations-south-africa) describes winter water-ice routes at Giant's Castle and Sani Pass (a commercial source, used only for 'ys'). Snow falls occasionally and often lies for days rather than all winter; see the next item for why this matters.

items.bewering: Daardie sneeu en ys smelt weer wanneer dit later warmer word. Die water loop dan by die berge af en dit vul die riviere.
items.blok: Waar water vries en weer smelt
items.bron: Wild Trout Association, after Prof. Colin Lewis, 'Physiography of the Kraai River Catchment' (https://www.wildtrout.co.za/index.php/eastern-cape-highlands/physiography-of-the-kraai-river-catchment): rivers rising on the Drakensberg escarpment 'are fed primarily by summer convectional thunderstorms', with 'occasional frontal rain and snowfall in winter'. UNESCO document (https://whc.unesco.org/document/154760): summer (Nov-Mar) brings 70% of annual rainfall, and winter is a distinct dry season. That snow melts and runs off is true. That it 'fills the rivers' is not: in the Drakensberg, rain fills them, and snowmelt from occasional falls adds a little. Every sentence is nearly true and the picture is false, since a learner concludes that South Africa's mountain rivers are filled by melting snow.
items.regstelling: Keep the melting and the runoff, and drop the claim that it fills the rivers, for example 'Die water loop dan by die berge af na die riviere toe.' or '...en dit loop in die riviere in.' Do not add any statement about how much river water comes from snow. Also consider 'Soms lê daar in die winter sneeu...', because the snow is occasional rather than lying all season.

items.bewering: Die klein druppels word groter en val as reën uit die wolk.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: UCI ESS5 Ch. 7 Precipitation (https://www.ess.uci.edu/~yu/class/ess5/Chapter.7.precipitation.pdf); UW-Madison 'How do raindrops form?' (https://wxguys.ssec.wisc.edu/2015/07/08/how-do-raindrops-form): droplets collide and coalesce until too large to stay suspended. Much mid-latitude rain also starts as ice crystals that melt, but the sentence describes a real route and does not claim it is the only one.

items.bewering: Swaartekrag trek die reën af, en die water loop oor die land.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: UCI ESS5 Ch. 7; USGS water cycle diagram (https://water.usgs.gov/edu/graphics/watercycle-usgs.pdf), which shows surface runoff.

items.bewering: Die reën wat val en die water in 'n rivier is albei 'n vloeistof. In hierdie stappe van die siklus beweeg die water, maar dit verander nie van toestand nie.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: USGS water cycle diagram (https://water.usgs.gov/edu/graphics/watercycle-usgs.pdf): precipitation as rain and runoff are transport of liquid water, with no phase change.

items.bewering: By die see verhit die son die water weer, en die siklus begin oor. Dieselfde water word oor en oor gebruik, en dit verdwyn nie.
items.blok: Die siklus begin van voor af
items.bron: ESA 'The water cycle' (https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2009/02/The_water_cycle) and 'Accounting for Earth's water' (https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2021/07/Accounting_for_Earth_s_water): the total stays essentially constant while its distribution shifts. Pacific Water, quoting USGS (https://pacificwater.org/pages.cfm/water-services/water-demand-management/water-distribution/the-water-cycle.html). Losses to space are negligible.

items.bewering: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.blok: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Sublimation and the water cycle' (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/sublimation-and-water-cycle): sublimation (snow and ice straight to vapour, which happens on snow-covered mountains) and deposition (vapour straight to ice, as in snowflakes and frost) are also water-cycle changes of state, and the USGS diagram labels both. The definite heading 'Die vier' presents the four as the complete set. That is false, and it bites in this lesson, which has snow on the Drakensberg.
items.regstelling: Heading only, no new content: make it non-exhaustive, for example 'Vier veranderings in die siklus'. Do not add sublimation or deposition to the lesson.

items.bewering: Verdamp: die son verhit die see en die riviere, en daardie water word waterdamp.
items.blok: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): evaporation takes water from the surface, not the whole body. The lesson's own study block says ''n deel daarvan verdamp'. A list item is revised on its own, and this one says the heated sea and river water becomes vapour, with no quantifier.
items.regstelling: Restore the quantifier the study block already carries, for example '...en 'n deel van daardie water word waterdamp.'

items.bewering: Kondenseer: die waterdamp koel hoër op af en word weer klein druppels water.
items.blok: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: RMI Belgium (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling); Penn State METEO 3 (lapse rate).

items.bewering: Vries: druppels vries hoog in 'n donderstorm en groei laag vir laag tot hael.
items.blok: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: NSSL Severe Weather 101: Hail (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail).

items.bewering: Smelt: sneeu en ys op hoë berge smelt wanneer dit warmer word.
items.blok: Die vier veranderings in die siklus
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, snow and ice pages (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/sublimation-and-water-cycle); UNESCO uKhahlamba-Drakensberg document for winter snow.

items.bewering: watersiklus: Dieselfde water se pad tussen die see, die lug en die land.
items.blok: watersiklus
items.bron: ESA 'The water cycle' (https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2009/02/The_water_cycle): circulation of a fixed amount of water among oceans, atmosphere and land. It holds read alone, and 'tussen' allows any order.

items.bewering: swaartekrag: Die krag wat alles na die aarde toe aftrek.
items.blok: swaartekrag
items.bron: Smithsonian NASM 'How Things Fly' (https://howthingsfly.si.edu/ask-an-explainer/what-gravity-7th-grade-words-and-understanding): gravity draws things toward Earth. It is a Grade 4 simplification of the universal attraction between masses, and it holds read alone.

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.blok: waterdamp
items.bron: Scientific American (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/how-does-bathwater-give-off-steam/); Science Buddies, ask-an-expert: water vapour is invisible.

items.bewering: wolk: Baie klein druppels water wat saam hoog in die lug hang.
items.blok: wolk
items.bron: NASA GPM FAQ (https://gpm.nasa.gov/resources/faq/what-are-clouds-made-are-they-more-likely-form-polluted-air-or-pristine-air): clouds are water drops, ice particles, or both, and high thin clouds are mostly ice. RMI Belgium (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling): cirrus is ice crystals only. Read alone, this entry defines every cloud as liquid droplets, which excludes ice clouds and the frozen top of the thunderstorm the lesson itself describes.
items.regstelling: Allow for ice, for example 'Baie klein druppels water of stukkies ys wat saam hoog in die lug hang.' It must match the study sentence in 'Hoër op kondenseer die waterdamp'. If 'wolk' is a shared definition for the subject, the change goes through the agreed-wording list, not only this lesson.

items.bewering: smelt: Wanneer 'n vaste stof warm word en in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.blok: smelt
items.bron: USGS Water Science School (https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/sublimation-and-water-cycle): melting is solid to liquid with heat. 'Warm word' reads as 'is heated'. Ice melting at 0 °C is not 'warm' in everyday terms, but the entry does not claim a temperature.

items.bewering: verdamp: Wanneer 'n vloeistof in 'n gas verander. Dit gebeur vinniger wanneer die vloeistof warmer is.
items.blok: verdamp
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Evaporation' (https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/process-evaporation): temperature affects how quickly evaporation happens.

items.bewering: kondenseer: Wanneer 'n gas afkoel en weer in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.blok: kondenseer
items.bron: RMI Belgium (https://www.meteo.be/nl/info/weerwoorden/wolkensamenstelling): cooling saturated vapour condenses to liquid droplets. 'Weer' assumes the gas was once a liquid, which is true for water vapour and harmless here.

items.bewering: vries: Wanneer 'n vloeistof afkoel en in 'n vaste stof verander.
items.blok: vries
items.bron: NSSL Severe Weather 101: Hail (https://nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail): liquid water freezes to ice on cooling below freezing.

opsomming: The lesson goes back to the writer for five fixes. The Drakensberg block says meltwater 'vul die riviere', but those rivers are filled mainly by summer thunderstorms and snow falls only occasionally. The cloud sentence and the 'wolk' glossary entry make a cloud droplets only, when clouds can be ice too, as the lesson's own hail cloud is. The list heading 'Die vier veranderings' presents four changes as the complete set. The 'Verdamp' list item drops the 'n deel' that its study block carries. The lesson has no superlatives and no explicit analogies; the 'pad' image was checked for its mapping and holds. Nothing is onseker.
